findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses AND instead of OR
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner. A team admin who is not the owner, or an owner who is not reported as an admin, fails the check. Unless they are also the organizer or an attendee, they get FORBIDDEN, even though the variable name says either role should be enough. Use || instead of &&.

findings.title: Scheduled emails sent to all input guests rather than only newly added ones
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails is passed `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`. If a submitted email was already an attendee, that existing attendee receives a fresh 'scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' notification. Pass uniqueGuests.

findings.title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive
findings.body: The blacklist entries are lowercased, but guest emails are compared as typed. Duplicate detection against existing attendees is also an exact-case comparison. A mixed-case variant of a blacklisted or existing email therefore bypasses both checks and gets added. Lowercase the guest emails before comparing.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials, not the organizer's
findings.body: EventManager is built from ctx.user and ctx.user's credentials. When an attendee or a team admin adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees runs with credentials that do not own the booking's calendar references. The update fails or throws, and because it is not caught, the request errors even though the attendee rows are already saved. Use the booking user's credentials (booking.user.credentials) instead.

findings.title: No restriction on cancelled or past bookings, and no limit on number of guests
findings.body: The handler does not check booking status. Any attendee can add an unbounded list of guests to any booking they belong to, including cancelled ones. Each added guest triggers outbound email, so this can be abused to spam arbitrary addresses.

findings.title: Error message fallback never applies
findings.body: The message is built with a template string that always produces a non-empty value, even when err.data is missing (e.g. 'undefined: ...'). As a result, the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback can never be used.
